subject: Proposal: Annual commit tiers + overage safeguard for FinLytics
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Kayla Martin <kayla@finlytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: Annual commit tiers + overage safeguard proposal

Hi Kayla —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I put together a concise annual commit structure that balances predictable cost for FinLytics with burst capacity and an overage safeguard so you don’t get hit by volatile month-to-month usage. Attached: commit_schedule_v1.xlsx and SLA_terms_draft.pdf.

High level (Starter / Growth / Enterprise):
- Starter: 50M tokens/year — 12% off list (hosted per-token price), includes 5% monthly burst pool (no charge up to pool).
- Growth: 250M tokens/year — 22% off list, includes 10% monthly burst pool + 20% discounted overage rate beyond pool.
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/year — 33% off list, dedicated routing and 15% burst pool, negotiated SLAs + 30% discounted overage.

Key protections we mentioned:
- Overage safeguard (smoothing credits): customers can apply unused commit in Q4 to offset peaks in Q1 per negotiated schedule.
- Safety valve: if usage exceeds 120% of committed monthly pacing, we step in with temporary throttling options and a one-week grace before any billed overage.
- DocuSign: if you want to move forward, I can send a formal SOW + commit addendum link.

Questions for you: 1) Which tier looks closest to how you expect 2026 consumption to map? 2) Are there specific compliance or billing constraints we should flag to Legal?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk this.

— Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0187

Attachments: commit_schedule_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_terms_draft.pdf (PDF)

From: Kayla Martin <kayla@finlytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: Annual commit tiers + overage safeguard proposal

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary and the files. A few immediate questions from our side:

1) Burst pool vs overage: For Growth tier the 10% burst pool + discounted overage is appealing, but can you clarify how the "discounted overage" is applied in months where the burst pool is already consumed earlier in the quarter? Will overage be charged at the discounted rate immediately or only after a three-month reconciliation window?

2) Smoothing credits: We like the idea of moving unused commit, but Finance will need a clean rule set for reconciliation and cutoffs. Can you propose a practical reconciliation cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and a cap on how much carryover is allowed?

3) SLA and data residency: Legal wants a simple confirmation that log retention and audit trails for our account can be stored in the us-west region only. Any limitations there?

Also — our procurement asked whether there's any flexibility on the Growth tier discount if we commit to a two-year contract instead of annual.

Would you be available tomorrow for a 30m to walk through these?

Best,
Kayla
Head of Platform Partnerships | FinLytics
kayla@finlytics.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: FinLytics questions re: commit structure (need guidance)

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding Kayla's reply. Highlights we need to land:
- Clarify burst pool vs overage mechanics and reconciliation cadence (Finance will want deterministic rules)
- Two-year discount ask (they may prefer multi-year)
- Data residency: confirm us-west-only retention and audit log availability

My suggested concessions:
- Growth: make the discounted overage rate apply immediately after the burst pool is depleted within the month, and reconcile monthly. Allow up to 20% of unused annual commit to be carried forward per quarter (cap at 50% annual carryover).
- For 2-year commit: add +3% incremental discount on top of Growth slab, with annual re-opportunity to renegotiate based on usage.
- Data residency: confirm we can restrict logs to us-west for hosted API (need infra confirmation).

Can you propose language and a final numbers block I can send back to Kayla?

— Alex

On attachments: commit_schedule_v1.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinLytics questions re: commit structure (need guidance)

Alex —

Agree with your framing, but recommend tightening numbers to reduce open negotiation. My suggested final offer:

- Starter: 50M tokens/yr — 12% off price — 5% monthly burst pool — no carryover.
- Growth: 250M tokens/yr — 24% off price — 10% monthly burst pool — overage rate = hosted list * 0.60 (i.e., 40% discount) applied immediately after pool is consumed; monthly reconciliation; carryover allowed up to 15% of unused annual commit per quarter (cap 45% annual).
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/yr — 34% off price — 15% monthly burst pool — overage rate = hosted list * 0.55; dedicated routing; reserved SLA credits.

Two-year sweetener: additional 3% off the slab for Growth and Enterprise, billed annually in arrears, with a clause to review at the 12-month mark.

Smoothing credits process (what to tell Finance): monthly reconciliation with rolling quarterly carryover accounting. Carryover credits expire after two quarters. All carryover is applied at quarter-ends against invoiceable usage.

Data residency: Ben — can you confirm us-west-only log retention is supported for hosted accounts that opt-in? If yes, add to the SLA addendum: "Customer logs and audit trails will be stored in the us-west region only; access controls and export procedures will follow Redwood standard safeguards."

If Ben confirms, I suggest finalizing language and I can bake this into commit_schedule_final.xlsx and send back to Kayla with a DocuSign link.

— Marissa
Revenue Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Final: FinLytics annual commit portfolio + overage safeguard (formal offer)

Hi Kayla —

Appreciate the thoughtful questions — attached is a concise final offer (commit_schedule_final.xlsx) reflecting what we discussed internally. Highlights:

1) Growth tier (recommended for FinLytics based on your usage profile):
   - 250M tokens/year at 24% off list price
   - 10% monthly burst pool; if the pool is consumed, overage is billed at 60% of list (applies immediately within the month)
   - Monthly reconciliation; carryover allowed up to 15% of unused annual commit each quarter (cap 45% annually); carryover expires after two quarters

2) Two-year option: +3% off Growth slab if you sign a 2-year commit (same mechanics; discounts applied per invoice year)

3) Smoothing & safety valve: temporary throttling at 120% of monthly pacing with a one-week grace; automated alerts and one-touch credits for SLA breaches per attached SLA_terms_draft.pdf

4) Data residency: Redwood confirms hosted logs/audit trails for your account can be restricted to the us-west region. We will include the exact wording in the addendum.

Next steps:
- I can generate a DocuSign packet (SOW + commit addendum). If Legal wants language tweaks, point them to the linked DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/finlytics/offer-8743.
- Let me know if you prefer the two-year sweetener and I’ll mark the quote accordingly.

If this looks good I’ll issue a formal DocuSign by EOD tomorrow. Happy to jump on a call if any open items remain.

Best regards,
Alex Martinez
